annotations.text:
1 · CUPERTINO — the safe one.
Stock macOS: translucent source-list sidebar, unified toolbar, SF type, Source/Rendered segmented control. Rendering is fully live — you never see the asterisks.
Tradeoff: looks like every other Mac app. Nothing here is yours.

2 · LEDGER — three panes, Mail/NetNewsWire lineage.
Folders, then a note list with two-line previews and MD/TXT badges, then the editor. Best of the five at answering "which file was that?" without opening anything.
Tradeoff: 484px gone before a word of text. Cramped under ~1100px wide.

3 · MANUSCRIPT — writing room, not file manager.
Warm paper, Newsreader serif at 18px, ~600px measure, chrome almost gone. Sidebar is a quiet stack of titles with word counts, no icons at all.
Tradeoff: weakest file chooser of the five, and serif suits prose far better than checklists or logs.

4 · SLATE — dark split view for people who think in source.
Raw markdown with line numbers and syntax tinting on the left, rendered on the right, scroll-synced. Sidebar shows md/txt as type tags plus a dirty dot.
Tradeoff: half your width is spent showing the same text twice.

5 · TERMINAL — hybrid live preview, the strongest opinion here.
Headers and bold render at size, but the #, ** and ` markers stay visible in dim grey, so you always edit the real file. Plex Mono throughout, indent-guide file tree, modal status bar.
Tradeoff: monospace body text is tiring to read long, and the vim vocabulary is a learned taste.

6 · MANUSCRIPT × LEDGER — the one you asked for.
Manuscript's palette and type (warm paper, Newsreader serif, rust accent, muted traffic lights) on Ledger's three-pane skeleton: folder list, note list with previews and MD/TXT badges, editor with breadcrumb, Preview/Source toggle and a word-count status bar.

What had to give: the editor pane is 716px instead of a full window, so the measure is 546px and the H1 drops from 40px to 35px. Section heads switched from serif to letterspaced small-caps sans — at 30px of vertical rhythm the serif version fought the note titles two panes over.

The toggle is Ledger's shape recoloured rust, not a Manuscript invention.

The first five are the original directions; 6 is the combination.

Every artboard shows the same note and the same file list on purpose — the only variable is style.

Mixed .md and .txt in every sidebar, since both have to be first-class.

These are static pictures — nothing clicks yet.
